text: Did the eraser itself leave a visible mark on the paper, rather than being used to erase something?
Was the message readable from pressure impressions made by the eraser, without adding pigment or erasing existing writing?
Did the message become visible because material on the eraser was deposited onto the paper?
Did rubbing with the eraser remove a coating or surface layer from the paper, making the message visible?
Was the message already present on or beneath the sheet before A used the eraser, and did the eraser merely reveal it?
Did A make the message visible as holes or tears in the paper?
Did A use the eraser to move or press a separate writing implement against the paper, with that implement making the message?
Did heat generated by rubbing the eraser cause the message to become visible?
Was the message formed by applying a marking substance to the paper while the eraser blocked part of it?
Was the paper light-sensitive, so that the eraser’s shadow helped make a message appear?
Did the eraser’s shape or pattern act as a printing die, with ink supplied separately and transferred to the paper?
Was the recipient meant to infer the message from where A placed the eraser, rather than from any change to the sheet?
Did the eraser chemically react with a separate substance on the paper to produce the message?
Was the object an ordinary stationery eraser, but used for a purpose other than erasing?
Did static charge from the eraser rearrange loose particles on the paper to form the message?

Did the device use a pen attached to an XY plotter mechanism to draw the pattern?

Did the eraser activate the device to draw a preset pattern, rather than guide the pen’s path?

Did rotation of a wheel mechanically drive the marking tool’s motion?

Did the eraser actuate a button or switch on the drawing device?
Did the device’s frame move by hand over the stationary paper while a mechanism within it constrained the marking tool’s path?

Did the device’s path over the paper correspond to the strokes of the intended message?

While the device drew, did the pencil’s detached eraser act as a spacer or support that kept the pencil in contact with the paper?
While the device drew, did A hold the detached pencil eraser in their hand to move the device?
Was the pencil’s attached eraser removed because its size or shape otherwise prevented the pencil from being secured in the drawing device?
Did A use the detached pencil eraser to help attach or position the pencil in the drawing device?
Before drawing, did A rub the detached pencil eraser against any part of the drawing device?
Did the detached pencil eraser contact the drawing device during setup, but not while A moved it to draw?
Was the detached pencil eraser used during setup to alter or adjust the drawing device?

A used the separate eraser while preparing a pencil for use in a drawing apparatus. The pencil served as the marking tool, fixed relative to the apparatus. A moved the apparatus by hand over the blank sheet, guiding the pencil along the strokes of the intended message. The pencil—not the eraser—made the marks; the eraser’s role was in preparing the pencil for the apparatus.

A used the separate eraser while preparing a pencil for the drawing apparatus, and a part of the pencil was removed. The pencil itself was then used as the marking tool, fixed relative to the apparatus. A moved the apparatus by hand over the stationary blank sheet along the strokes of the intended message, so the pencil—not the eraser—made the marks. The precise role of the separate eraser in preparing the pencil is unclear.
Did the separate eraser increase friction against the pencil’s attached eraser while A pulled it off?
Was the separate eraser essential for gripping the pencil’s attached eraser during removal, rather than merely incidental?
While A moved the apparatus to draw, was the pencil’s detached eraser physically fastened to it, rather than merely touching it?
